admission.transaction: Existing main() runtime(shared) -> canonical task(exclusive) -> TaskStore/audit ordering remains held through commit. command_assign reads raw runtime admission state in that transaction before changing roles, generation or emitting assignment audit.
rejects: Nonterminal task worker, including expired or missing-PID leases awaiting settlement

admission.settlement: Retained worker completed/failed/superseded and queue completed/failed records allow reassignment once launch reservations have settled. Retained worktree allocation metadata alone is not an active worker lease. Older unsettled generations are conservatively fenced too.
unchanged: Existing assignment CAS and generation increment
Supervisor pre-spawn, receipt and worker generation fences
Scheduler ordering/capacity, queue format, retry policy, providers and authentication

lease_first.proof: Forked launcher uses production start_worker_for_request under the real runtime admission lock. A local test adapter spawns a real bounded child process; production code persists a generation-1 worker lease. The separate operator process calls main() after the lease barrier and is rejected. TaskStore snapshot and assignment audit stay unchanged. The child is collected with terminal exit 0.

assignment_first.proof: Before main() commits reassignment, a second process attempts exclusive runtime admission and gets BlockingIOError, proving the lock remains held through the commit boundary. After generation 2 commits, the old detached generation-1 plan is queued. Production process_queue marks it completed/stale_dispatch_event, never builds an adapter, and creates no worker.

race_orderings.test_boundaries: These isolated process tests mock identity/config bootstrap and use a local adapter, with real locks, runtime files, main(), TaskStore and audit writes. They do not activate a live runtime or use production provider credentials. Existing real CLI assignment/reopen regressions also pass.
